items.title: probabilityStringMatch.js
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-12: "Add one item: probabilityStringMatch.js"

The goal: three core modules in run/js, probabilit<Name>.js, built one by one; their integration argued after.

THE SPEC, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"probabilityStringMatch is to work like this

result probability = probabilityStringMatch(A,B) where A and B must be strings.

{

 function helperFoo1() // from old gradedSearch-logic
 function helperFoo2() // form old logic
 ... etc.

if A or B are not of type string return 0.0;
if A is EXACTLY equal to B return 1.0

shorterString = the shorter String of A and B
longerString = longer String of A and B

if they are of equal length, shorterString = A, longerString = B,

then use the logic from gradedSearch to return a result between 0 and 1

}"

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-12)
- "in this version, we just compute the matching of two string, no matter which one is the search string." So no wildcards: * and ? are characters like any other.
- The reading confirmed by it: both folded (case, accents); shorter and longer as the spec says; no match 0.0; else the weighted mean of gradedSearch's four signals (match 1.0, coverage 0.2, tokens 0.3, sequence 0.25), the helpers copied in, gradedSearch.js untouched until the integration.
- "and empty string against a non-empty string should return 0"

FOUND
- search today: bucket.js, searchBucket.js, gradedSearch.js, nodeSearches.js, peerSearch.js in run/js; a new file there is core, so its commit needs his grant.

items.title: probabilityStringObjectMatch
items.box:
Andy, 2026-10-12: "new Item probabilityStringObjectMatch"

The goal: three core modules in run/js, probabilit<Name>.js, built one by one; their integration argued after. The first, probabilityStringMatch(A, B), is built (goal/G18.2, a9a0c252).

THE SPEC, proposed, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"this one we'll discuss a little bit

function probabilityStringObjectMatch(string,object){

1. the input must be valid string and object, empty string will return 0,

2. We "measure" the object
let table = [{objectString, weight]
function measureObject(){
// this internal function extracts every valid string from the object and places it in a table of objects, which contain the string and an empty weight (0.0) for staters
}

3. we assign weight to each string as follows: this is proposed and will be discussed.
the shortest string in the object gets the highest weight, the longest string in the object gets the smallest weight, and all the weights of the string in the table must add up to 1.0,

4. the overall input string is then matched agains all strings in the object, using pobabilityStringMatch(). each of those results is then multiplied by the weight of the corresponding object-string, and added to the overall result.

5. the overall result is returned.
}

thoughts?"

DECIDED, Andy, 2026-10-12:
"1. agreed. empty string stay out of the table.

2. no arrays are searched in this version.

3. dilution concern. when searching a table of objects, dilution doesn't matter because we look for the best matching contact not for the perfect one (this will become obvious in our 3rd item: probabilityBucket)"
- "nested objects will be searched for strings to put into the table."
- The weights: "you formula-correction is accepted." Each string weighs (S - L) / S / (n - 1), S the added length of all its strings, n how many; one string alone weighs 1.0; they add up to 1, the shortest heaviest.
- "if keys are string, they are included, this is supposed to be "dumb"": every key of the object and its nested objects goes into the table with the values (keys are always strings), empty ones out.

checks.words: How should probabilityStringObjectMatch work: a string against an object, for example the best probabilityStringMatch over the object values?
Weighted sum as proposed, or the best match?
And the weights: proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1, is that your shortest-heaviest?
That, and still open: values only, or the keys too?

How should probabilityStringObjectMatch work: a string against an object, for example the best probabilityStringMatch over the object values?

Workable, with three gaps: empty strings must stay out of the table (shortest means heaviest, and they always match 0); does every valid string mean nested objects and arrays too, and the keys or only the values; and weight proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1, is the plainest shortest-heaviest.
One concern: a weighted sum dilutes a perfect hit, so a name matched exactly among nine other fields scores about 0.2 and can lose to an object that matches everything weakly; the best weighted match would not.
Weighted sum as proposed, or the best match?

2. no arrays are searched in this version.

3. dilution concern. when searching a table of objects, dilution doesn't matter because we look for the best matching contact not for the perfect one (this will become obvious in our 3rd item: probabilityBucket)

Recorded (v3): empty strings out, no arrays, the weighted sum stands since the bucket picks the best of many.
Open: does it go into nested plain objects, and are keys strings of the object or only values?
And the weights: proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1, is that your shortest-heaviest?
nested objects will be searched for strings to put into the table.

Recorded: nested objects are searched, arrays not.
Two left: only the values, or the keys too (a contact {name: "ann"} would then also match "name"); and the weights proportional to 1/length, scaled to add up to 1.
Values only, and 1/length, yes?

for the weights of the strings:

1. the added length of all strings in the object represents 1.0
the weight of a single string is

 (sumOfAllSringLengthsAdded - stringLength) / sumOfAllSringLengthsAdded 

is this a viable formula?

Viable with one change: (S - L)/S over n strings adds up to n - 1, not 1 (lengths 3, 7, 10 give 0.85, 0.65, 0.5, sum 2), so each is divided by n - 1: 0.425, 0.325, 0.25, sum 1, shortest heaviest; with two strings it is already right.
One string alone gives (S - L)/S = 0, so a single string takes the whole weight, 1.0.
That, and still open: values only, or the keys too?

you formula-correction is accepted.

if keys are string, they are included, this is supposed to be "dumb"
